# GORM

Promise: Model how things connect.

GORM is a strongly typed graph ORM for .NET and SQL Server Graph with explicit nodes and edges, LINQ-style traversal, relationship-aware loading, change tracking, graph mutations, in-memory execution and temporal history.

Canonical site: https://pjotrcasteel.github.io/GORM/
Canonical repository: https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/GORM

- Interactive LINQ to SQL playground: https://pjotrcasteel.github.io/GORM/playground.html

## Core model

Nodes are ordinary domain entities that participate in graph topology. Edges are typed directed relationships and may carry their own properties. Id is the default identity convention. Queries begin from Set<TNode>() and use familiar LINQ until graph-specific intent is needed.

Key documented query operations include:
- Set<TNode>()
- Where / Select / OrderBy / Skip / Take and aggregates
- Outgoing<TEdge,TTarget>()
- Incoming<TEdge,TSource>()
- Include(...) / ThenInclude(...)
- WhereId(...) / WhereIds(...)
- AsOf(...), Current() and temporal range operations
- async materialization such as ToListAsync(), SingleAsync() and CountAsync()

## Runnable documentation

GORM query code blocks in the documentation can open directly in the playground. The runnable examples catalog provides focused traversal, paging, temporal and relationship-loading scenarios.

The Graph Model Explorer is a visual learning tool for graph topology and traversal direction. A user chooses a root node and follows typed edges; the explorer emits the equivalent Outgoing<TEdge,TTarget>() or Incoming<TEdge,TSource>() chain and a matching SQL Server Graph shape. Generated explorer queries can open directly in the playground for further editing and translation inspection.

The playground supports shareable custom-query permalinks. A permalink preserves the editor query so it can be used in documentation, issue reports and pull request discussions. It does not imply that the generated SQL is authoritative runtime output while the real translator is still pending source migration.

## Advanced capabilities

Implementation materials also describe deeper capabilities over the same GORM graph runtime:
- Graph Intelligence for centrality, routing, components, communities and impact analysis;
- Temporal Digital Twin simulation and isolated what-if scenarios;
- Explainable GraphRAG with path-aware graph evidence and explicit security boundaries;
- Helix query analysis, generated SQL inspection and safe optimization;
- a ChangeSet and transaction compiler for inspectable ordered writes, rollback semantics and concurrency conflicts.

These are documented as capabilities, not as guaranteed public signatures. Exact namespaces, method signatures and package boundaries must be validated after source migration.

## Playground status

The public repository does not yet contain the migrated GORM expression visitor and SQL generator. The browser playground is therefore explicitly a documentation preview translator for focused query shapes. It visualizes query anatomy, translation stages, bind parameters, diagnostics and expected SQL Server Graph concepts but must not be treated as the production translator.

The playground UI is intentionally separated from the translator implementation. `playground-adapter.js` resolves an optional `window.GormPlaygroundEngine` and otherwise falls back to `playground-preview-engine.js`. A translator exposes metadata plus `translate(query)` and returns an object containing at least `ok`, `sql` and `model`; `notes` is optional UI context. This is the integration boundary the migrated .NET translator should implement through a sandboxed adapter.

Six documentation contracts cover outgoing traversal, incoming traversal, chained traversal, filter/paging, temporal AsOf and Include. CI validates JavaScript syntax, internal documentation links/routes and these translator contracts on pull requests and main-branch documentation changes.

## Repository status

The public repository identity is GORM. Implementation source migration and NuGet publication are intentionally deferred until organization-specific naming is removed, public symbols are validated and the complete .NET 10 build/test/performance suite is green.

## Boundary

GORM owns graph mapping, query translation, change tracking, graph history and graph persistence mechanics. Analysis, preview and simulation remain read-only unless the application explicitly invokes a mutation or save operation. Business policy remains application-owned.
